answer: Unique answer proof. Each identity must submit a nonce whose hash, under a public epoch salt, meets a fixed difficulty target and whose full answer string is absent from a global ledger; duplicates and ledger collisions are rejected. The challenge salt changes per epoch, like a tide over a reef, so precomputed answers expire. An attacker must pay the expected 2^d hash trials per identity, plus a ledger lookup, to mint N distinct answers. A mesa-sized batch therefore costs N times that work, not one reusable answer. No fable of shared identity helps,
